CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 14, audited at commit 873d8c2 (HEAD of the main checkout, tree
fd1ea1f7...). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. One requirement unmet, one uncommitted change that must not
be committed. The revert itself is exactly right.

THE REVERT IS PROVABLY CLEAN, and it is worth leading with because it settles four
criteria at once:

    git diff --stat 080ce1e HEAD   ->   empty

The committed tree is byte-identical to Sprint 12's. That is the strongest possible
evidence for R1, R2, R3 and R4 simultaneously and it needs no interpretation: there
can be no orphaned import, no dead style reference, no leftover dependency, and
lib/ephemeris/ cannot have drifted, because there is no difference at all. Sprint 13's
three artifacts are gone, actions.ts is back to its 080ce1e form with server-side
randomUUID intact, and Sprint 12's engine is untouched by construction rather than by
inspection. I confirmed the consequences independently anyway: 110 tests pass (Sprint
12's count, so Sprint 13's nine are gone and nothing else went with them), npm ci on
a clean export of HEAD resolves cleanly at 522 packages, lint and typecheck exit 0.

REQUIRED FIX 1 -- R8 is not met, and the byte-identical tree is why.

R8: "README.md reflects the reverted UI, and records why the aspect engine is retained
while unused -- otherwise the next reader deletes it as dead code." The risk register
repeats it: "The aspect engine gets deleted as dead code ... with the reason written
into the README rather than living only here."

README at HEAD does not mention the aspect engine at all -- I grepped for "aspect" and
got nothing. It cannot: a byte-perfect revert to 080ce1e restores 080ce1e's README,
and that note is new work this sprint was asked to add. The first half of R8 is
satisfied for free (the reverted README describes the text-only page, which is what
/chart is again); the second half is missing entirely.

This is not carelessness, and I want that on the record, because the sprint file's own
two criteria pull against each other. R1's criterion says the diff "undoes 2fb6062 and
9b132e3 and nothing else. Any change not attributable to reverting those two commits
fails this criterion," and it is flagged as "the criterion that keeps a revert a
revert." R8 requires a README addition that is, by definition, not attributable to
reverting those two commits. Read R1 literally -- and it is written to be read
literally -- and you produce exactly this commit. The resolution is that R8's note is
requested work and therefore attributable to this sprint, not an improvement smuggled
in, but the sprint file does not say so and someone had to guess. Worth reconciling
the two criteria so the next revert sprint does not re-run this.

What the note needs to say is already written in the sprint file: the engine is
retained deliberately because the next phase's data model is expected to consume it,
and deleting tested working code to re-derive it in three weeks is the worse trade.
A short paragraph. Nothing else in README should move.

REQUIRED FIX 2 -- an uncommitted dependency addition that is not part of this revert.

The working tree carries an uncommitted change to package.json and package-lock.json:

    +    "@supabase/ssr": "^0.12.4",

Nothing in the repository imports it. I grepped app/ and lib/ for it and the only
hits anywhere are inside my own archived audit notes in docs/sprints/state/*.json,
which are text, not code. Its history explains it: git log -S shows @supabase/ssr
entered at 0251e99 (Sprint 3, the aborted auth sprint) and left at f90429a (that
sprint's revert). It has not been in package.json since, and Sprint 13 never added it
-- Sprint 13's diff did not touch package.json at all.

So this is an unused dependency from a different aborted sprint being re-added during a
revert sprint whose first criterion is "nothing else." If it gets committed, R1's
criterion fails on its own terms, and the "while we're in there" risk the sprint file
names lands on the one sprint least able to absorb it. Drop it -- git checkout
package.json package-lock.json -- or, if there is a reason for it I cannot see from
here, that reason belongs in the sprint file as a recorded deviation the way R7's was
in Sprint 13, not in an uncommitted diff.

Note that the committed pair is currently consistent: npm ci against HEAD's
package.json and lockfile succeeds. Committing only one of the two would break that.

Requirements coverage:
R1 MET. See above -- the diff is empty against 080ce1e.
R2 MET. No surviving reference to chart.module.css or constellation in app/, lib/ or
  README. The two grep hits on "constellation" are comments in
  lib/ephemeris/aspects.ts and julian-day.test.ts citing
  docs/design/HANDOFF_chart_constellation.md, which still exists -- Sprint 12 files
  referencing a design document, not orphaned pointers at deleted code.
R3 MET. actions.ts is at its 080ce1e form: randomUUID from node:crypto under
  "use server", and the insert error returns rather than being swallowed.
R4 MET, by tree identity. lib/ephemeris/ is byte-identical to 080ce1e, aspects.ts,
  balance.ts, julian-day.ts and moon-phase.ts all present, and their tests still run
  in the default suite rather than being skipped -- the 110-test count is the proof,
  since 39 of those are the adapter's and 15 the aspect engine's.
R5 MET. next.config.ts still declares the / -> /chart redirect, and
  app/api/health/db/route.ts still imports getDeployedCommit and includes commit in
  all three response branches.
R6 MET. The no-listing-route guardrail (13 tests) and ci-guardrails (3) are intact
  and green, and supabase/tests/ is unchanged, so the RLS suite is still wired into
  the rls-tests job.
R7 MET. git diff 080ce1e HEAD -- supabase/ is empty. Five migrations, unchanged, none
  added. No DDL anywhere in the diff.
R8 NOT MET. See required fix 1.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 110 tests across 11 files.
- npm ci --dry-run on a pristine git archive of HEAD: exit 0, 522 packages, so the
  committed package.json and lockfile agree with each other.

Notes, not conditions:
1. GroundTruth's fixture criterion is the sharpest thing in this sprint file and it
   deserves saying out loud: the fixture reading was captured from production at
   9b132e3 with its expected values written down, not just its URL, and it cannot be
   recreated once this ships. That is the right instinct -- "it loads" is not the same
   as "it is right", and the failure mode named there, a silently altered number, is
   exactly what a static gate cannot see. I can confirm /reading/[id] is byte-identical
   to its 080ce1e form and that no schema changed, which is the whole static case for
   why the fixture should render unchanged. It is not proof. The comparison is
   GroundTruth's and it should be done value by value against the table in the sprint
   file, not by eye.
2. Sprint 12's applying/separating lookahead question is now moot for the product --
   nothing renders A/S any more. The engine still computes it, and whatever consumes
   the engine next will inherit the same one-day-step decision. My Sprint 12
   measurement stands on the record for whoever picks it up: about one verdict in nine
   differs between a one-day and a one-hour lookahead, and the shorter step is the
   correct one.
3. saveReading still discards the Supabase error object rather than logging it,
   carried since Sprint 10 and restored intact by this revert. Correct for a revert --
   fixing it here would be exactly the scope creep R1 exists to prevent. Worth
   carrying into the next phase's sprint rather than losing.

Re-audit after both fixes. Fix 1 is a paragraph in README; fix 2 is discarding an
uncommitted change. Keep the re-audit proportionate -- the revert itself is right and
nothing in the code should move.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 14, round 2. Audited at commit 1dd1e9d, HEAD of the main checkout,
recorded tree 2baca207... Sprint file re-read fresh, including the 22 Aug amendment to
the R1/R2/R3 criterion.

VERDICT: PASS.

REQUIRED FIX 1 -- R8. FIXED. README now names all four retained modules
(aspects.ts, balance.ts, moon-phase.ts, julian-day.ts), says what they compute, says
plainly that nothing in the UI calls them, and gives the reason they stay: the next
phase's data model is expected to consume them, and re-deriving tested working code
later is the worse trade. It also records that the UI which used them was reverted
ahead of a data-model revision "not because this code was wrong", which is the
sentence that actually stops a tidy-minded reader deleting it. Sited directly above
the vestigial-columns paragraph, which is the right neighbourhood -- that section is
now where this repository keeps its deliberate-looking-like-dead-code decisions.

REQUIRED FIX 2 -- the uncommitted @supabase/ssr addition. FIXED, by dropping it.
git diff against package.json and package-lock.json is empty, and the committed
package.json carries no @supabase/ssr. The working tree is clean apart from sprint
bookkeeping and one new untracked file, see note 2.

THE R1 RECHECK, which is the whole point of a revert sprint:

    git diff --stat 080ce1e HEAD   ->   README.md | 8 ++++++++

Eight added lines, and they are exactly the R8 paragraph. Nothing else in the entire
tree differs from Sprint 12's state. That is precisely what the amended criterion
asks for -- the two reverts plus exactly the README paragraph R8 requires, and
nothing else -- and it is verifiable in one command rather than by reading a diff and
forming an impression.

On the amendment itself: the sprint file now reconciles R1 and R8 with a dated note
that states the distinction (R8's note is work the sprint asks for and is therefore
attributable to it; an improvement to the restored page is not) and attributes the
contradiction to the sprint file rather than to Dev Team. That is the right fix in the
right place, and it means the next revert sprint inherits the resolution instead of
re-deriving it.

Requirements coverage:
R1/R2/R3 MET. See the recheck above. actions.ts is unchanged from 080ce1e, so
  randomUUID stays server-side under "use server" and the insert error still returns
  rather than being swallowed.
R2 MET. No surviving reference to chart.module.css or constellation in app/, lib/ or
  README. package.json carries nothing Sprint 13 introduced -- Sprint 13 never touched
  it, and the Sprint 3 leftover flagged in round 1 is gone.
R4 MET, by direct comparison rather than inference: git diff 080ce1e HEAD --
  lib/ephemeris is empty. The four modules and their tests are byte-identical, and
  still wired into the default suite rather than skipped -- 110 tests across 11 files,
  15 of them the aspect engine's and 39 the adapter's.
R5 MET, verified live. Started the built app: GET / returns 307 to /chart, and
  /api/health/db returns its commit block with sha and short populated from
  VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA.
R6 MET. The no-listing-route guardrail (13 tests) and ci-guardrails (3) are green, and
  supabase/tests/ is byte-identical, so the RLS suite is still wired into rls-tests.
R7 MET. git diff 080ce1e HEAD -- supabase/ is empty. Five migrations, none added, no
  DDL anywhere in the diff.
R8 MET. See required fix 1.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 110 tests across 11 files.
- next build exits 0. Route table: /_not-found, /api/health/db, /chart (back to
  dynamic, correct for a server component reading searchParams), /reading/[id].
- Served the built app: / redirects, /chart?date=... renders the text-only table, and
  the health endpoint reports its commit.

AND ONE THING I DID NOT EXPECT TO BE ABLE TO CHECK. The sprint file records the
GroundTruth fixture's expected values rather than just its URL, which made them
testable from here. I served the reverted build, requested /chart?date=1977-03-31 --
the fixture's date, at the same noon-UTC convention the save used -- and compared all
ten rows against the table in the sprint file:

  Sun Aries 10.66 / Moon Leo 22.45 / Mercury Aries 25.52 / Venus Aries 19.87 R /
  Mars Pisces 8.90 / Jupiter Taurus 29.39 / Saturn Leo 10.05 R / Uranus Scorpio 10.95 R
  / Neptune Sagittarius 16.09 R / Pluto Libra 12.88 R

All ten match exactly -- sign, degree to two decimals, and retrograde flag.

Be precise about what that does and does not establish. The fixture's values are what
/reading/[id] rendered from the STORED row at 9b132e3, so a fresh computation matching
them means Sprint 13's save path stored correct positions -- which is exactly the risk
the sprint file names ("Sprint 13's save-path changes silently dropped something").
That risk is now substantially retired from the static side. What remains untested is
the row itself: whether that specific id still reads back and renders on the reverted
deploy. /reading/[id] is byte-identical to its 080ce1e form and no schema changed, so
there is no mechanism for it to differ -- but "no mechanism I can see" is not the same
as "checked", and checking it is GroundTruth's, not mine. The comparison should still
be done value by value against the live page.

Notes, not conditions:
1. Sprint 12's applying/separating lookahead is moot for the product now -- nothing
   renders A/S. The engine still computes it and whatever consumes it next inherits
   the same one-day-step decision. The measurement stands on the record: roughly one
   verdict in nine differs between a one-day and a one-hour lookahead, and the shorter
   step is the correct one. Worth carrying into the next phase's sprint file rather
   than leaving it in an audit note nobody re-reads.
2. docs/design/CHART_MODEL.md is new and untracked. It is not in the audited tree and
   not part of this sprint, so it does not affect this verdict -- flagging it only so
   it does not get swept into the shipped commit the way the @supabase/ssr change
   nearly was. If it belongs to the forthcoming data-model work, it should land with
   that sprint.
3. saveReading still discards the Supabase error object rather than logging it,
   restored intact by the revert. Correct here -- fixing it would have been the scope
   creep R1 exists to prevent -- and still worth a line in the next phase's sprint.

Cleared to ship at 1dd1e9d. Standing note for Pipeman: files under docs/sprints/ are

PASS: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 14, commit
1dd1e9de8936f8fc207fe6800a3d0f782db1d090.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-22 ~17:30Z.

VERDICT: PASS. All four criteria verified. The surface is server-rendered again,
so everything this sprint claims was testable with the tools I have -- which was
not true of Sprint 13.

CRITERION 1 -- the fixture reading still opens and renders identically. PASS.
This is the sprint's actual proof, and it is the one that could never be re-tested
later: no one can create another Sprint-13-era row now that the revert is live.
  GET /reading/f8d046f7-6432-4961-b996-d65c9f623a8e -> HTTP/2 200, no Set-Cookie.
  Heading: "Reading for 1977-03-31" -- matches.
  Compared value by value against the captured fixture, not eyeballed. All ten
  bodies match on sign, degree AND retrograde flag:
    Sun Aries 10.66 No | Moon Leo 22.45 No | Mercury Aries 25.52 No |
    Venus Aries 19.87 Yes | Mars Pisces 8.90 No | Jupiter Taurus 29.39 No |
    Saturn Leo 10.05 Yes | Uranus Scorpio 10.95 Yes |
    Neptune Sagittarius 16.09 Yes | Pluto Libra 12.88 Yes
  Zero mismatches across 30 compared values plus the heading. The sprint file was
  right that "should render" was doing real work in that sentence -- so I checked
  every number rather than confirming a 200.

  I ALSO CHECKED SOMETHING THE CRITERION DID NOT ASK FOR, because this row is now
  the only surviving artifact of Sprint 13's save path and it is permanent: are
  the stored values actually CORRECT, or merely stably wrong? A row written by an
  aborted sprint could render identically forever and still be nonsense.
  Verified against NASA JPL Horizons (geocentric, ecliptic-of-date) for
  1977-03-31 12:00 UT, with retrograde derived independently from motion between
  1977-03-30 and 1977-04-01:
    worst longitude error 31.2 arcsec (0.0087 deg), at display rounding
    all ten signs correct
    all five retrograde flags correct (Venus, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto)
    zero mismatches
  So Sprint 13's save path wrote astronomically correct data before the sprint was
  abandoned. The fixture is a good fixture, not just a stable one.

CRITERION 2 -- / redirects to /chart, /chart serves the text-only page, a date
produces positions. PASS.
  GET / -> HTTP/2 307, location: /chart (Sprint 11's redirect unaffected, R5).
  GET /chart?date=2024-03-20 -> 200, and the date is a server-read query parameter
  again. This is the concrete difference from Sprint 13, where the identical URL
  returned the empty state and the results existed only in the client.
  Text-only confirmed by absence, not assumption: 0 <svg> elements, 0 occurrences
  of "constellation" anywhere in the served HTML.
  Positions rendered:
    Sun Aries 0.37 | Moon Leo 8.29 | Mercury Aries 17.97 | Venus Pisces 10.63 |
    Mars Aquarius 28.06 | Jupiter Taurus 14.96 | Saturn Pisces 12.27 |
    Uranus Taurus 20.27 | Neptune Pisces 27.48 | Pluto Aquarius 1.67
  Byte-identical to the values I verified against JPL Horizons in Sprint 6 (worst
  20.4 arcsec) and saw again in Sprint 12. The revert restored the pre-Sprint-13
  behaviour without moving a number. Instant still stated:
  2024-03-20T12:00:00.000Z.

CRITERION 3 -- saving returns a link, and opening it in a fresh session with no
cookies renders the reading. PASS. Sprint 10's round trip survived the revert.
  POST the save action -> HTTP/2 303,
    location: /reading/8434c0e9-90b1-4701-8be9-97b11003ae1e
  GET that link with no cookie jar -> 200, no Set-Cookie, rendered server-side:
    "Reading for 2024-03-20 | Sun Aries 0.37 No | Moon Leo 8.29 No | ...
     Pluto Aquarius 1.67 No" -- matching the chart page it was saved from.
  Detail worth recording as evidence of a genuine revert rather than a reimplement:
  the server action id is $ACTION_ID_407e47aa4d86ae8cc43c2f973ad6092d071cd959b0 --
  byte-identical to the one I drove in Sprint 10. R3 asked for actions.ts restored
  to its 080ce1e form and that is what the wire shows.
  Save failures still surface (R3/R6): POST with date=1699-12-31 -> 303 to
  /chart?date=1699-12-31&error=Date%20must%20be%20between%201700-01-01%20and%202100-12-31.
  No success state, no reading created.

CRITERION 4 -- /api/health/db reports the shipped commit. PASS.
  {"status":"ok","connected":true,
   "migrationVersion":"20260816181929_readings_positions_not_null",
   "commit":{"sha":"1dd1e9de8936f8fc207fe6800a3d0f782db1d090",
             "short":"1dd1e9d","isLocal":false}}
  Matches Pipeman's ship and origin/main exactly, all 40 characters.

OTHER CHECKS
  - Sprint 10's negative guarantees intact (R6): /readings 404, /api/readings 404,
    freshly generated random reading id 404.
  - R2, Sprint 13's artifacts removed: app/chart/ on origin/main now contains only
    actions.ts and page.tsx. chart.module.css, constellation.ts and

  - CI green on this commit (run 32587162585, 17:15Z): build, rls-tests and

A LOOSE END I RAISED EARLIER, NOW CLOSED. On 16 Aug I flagged that the Supabase
access token then in use was set to expire 22 Aug 2026 -- today -- and that CI's
migrate job would break with a different-looking error. That token was replaced
the same day (SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN last updated 2026-08-16T12:44:29Z, the
full-access replacement), and migrate passed today at 17:15Z. So the specific
expiry I warned about is moot. I cannot see the replacement's expiry date from
here; if it also carries one, the same trap is still armed, just on an unknown
date. Worth someone checking once rather than rediscovering it.

ON THE TOOLING GAP. Sprint 13's CONDITIONAL was recorded because the product's
primary surface had moved behind JavaScript and this session has no browser. That
sprint is now aborted and reverted, so the gap is not blocking anything today:
every criterion here was verifiable over plain HTTP, and I verified all of them.
The gap is dormant, not fixed. Any future sprint that client-renders the chart
puts the live gate back where Sprint 13 left it, and the honest options then are
the same two: give a GroundTruth session a browser, or scope the criteria to what
can actually be observed and say why.

TEST DATA. This test added one production row,
8434c0e9-90b1-4701-8be9-97b11003ae1e (2024-03-20), by exercising the save path
criterion 3 requires. Anon cannot delete, so it persists like the others. Running
count of rows this role has left in production across the exercise: four.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks
are curl over HTTPS against production, the JPL Horizons HTTP API as reference,
and the gh CLI for CI state. No JavaScript was executed and no rendering observed
-- which for this commit costs nothing, because the pages are server-rendered.
